thread:
amelia (support): 🚨 multiple customers reporting 503s for live streaming endpoints since ~03:40 UTC. high impact: streaming sessions drop mid-response. seeing runner restarts + container restarts on hosted-gpu-pool-07. escalating for triage

jordan (cs): which customers / sample request_ids? I can surface to CS if we have repros

amelia (support): cust: fintax-inc, quickchatlab. example req_id: r_0a9f3c (reported at 03:41 UTC). both are streaming toolcall sessions with long-running audio->text->toolcall loops.

raj (oncall): inference-bot posted alerts:

inference-bot: [ALERT] upstream-runner crashloop detected on hosted-gpu-pool-07 (3 hosts). crash_reason: SIGSEGV | crash_count: 27 in 12m | avg restart latency: 4s

devon (infra): pulling runner logs now. initial findings: repeated OOM-ish memory growth then segfault in attention kernel. attaching trimmed log:```
Runner[3241]: GPU memory 15872/16384 MB
Runner[3241]: kv_cache_alloc: growing to 12.1GB
Runner[3241]: entering attention kernel (seq_len=8192)
Runner[3241]: FAILED: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
Runner[3241]: signal 11 (SIGSEGV) at 0x7f3b2c0
backtrace: 0x7f3b2c0 -> 0x7f2a1b4 -> 0x55a1c0
container: paused, restarting
```

sophia (sre): This pattern looks like a memory leak or unbounded kv cache growth under streaming with toolcalls. The long contexts + toolcall outputs are causing kv_prefetch to allocate more than expected and not free between segments. p95 mem climbs until kernel crashes.

raj (oncall): Can we reproduce locally? steps I used:```
# reproduce (approx)
export REDWOOD_ENV=staging
curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/v1/stream \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-hf","stream":true,"input":"<long prompt with many tool calls>"}'
```
I ran a sustained stream for ~6 minutes and saw kv cache grow steadily.

devon (infra): repro confirmed on a small repro host with smaller GPU: GPU mem climbs ~200MB/min when toolcalls return large embeddings and we don't evict prefixes. After ~7 minutes we hit device OOM and runner SIGSEGV.

amelia (support): customers also reported "auth token invalid" errors immediately before 503s. could the token refresh flow be triggering extra retries that blow up memory?

raj (oncall): Good catch — we observed many duplicate requests from the same session during toolcall retries (client resending on short timeouts). That increases effective concurrency and kv retention.

devon (infra): Immediate mitigations I'm trying now:
- throttle streaming concurrency for hosted-gpu-pool-07 (reduce max streams per-GPU to 4)
- enable aggressive kv_cache eviction (experimental flag kv_eviction_aggressiveness=2)
- route toolcalls to a fallback non-gpu variant for streaming paths (model_variant=quant-cpu)
I'll post results in 5–10m.

sophia (sre): Add a temporary global rate-limit on authenticated streaming endpoints for impacted customers to stop retries spiraling. CS, please notify customers.

jordan (cs): notif drafted, will send: "We're rate-limiting streaming sessions temporarily while we stabilize. We're investigating an upstream runner crash that can drop responses; we'll share repro and ETA." :thumbsup:

devon (infra): quick patch rolled to staging: kv_cache will now cap per-session prefix memory to 1.2GB and force eviction on toolcall boundary. patch id: pr-7893. Rolling to hosted-gpu-pool-07 in 2m.

inference-bot: [INFO] pr-7893 deployed to hosted-gpu-pool-07 (canary on host-07b). monitoring for regressions.

amelia (support): any logs / traces we should capture from affected customers to help postmortem?

raj (oncall): ask for:
- full request_id(s)
- raw toolcall payloads (size, number of nested calls)
- whether client retried on 4xx/5xx and how many retries
- if they saw duplicate streaming frames
Also capture host GPU memory timeline from metrics (agent: host_exporter.gpu_mem.used by minute).

devon (infra): current status: canary host-07b stopped crashing after pr-7893, crashcount -> 0 in 8m. host-07a still noisy, continuing drain + force-patch. If canary holds, we'll promote and keep rate limits until next deploy.

sophia (sre): next steps for postmortem:
- reproduce with deterministic large nested toolcall + retry pattern
- add guardrails: per-session kv cap, toolcall-response-size limit, backpressure when kv pressure high
- add alert for kv_cache growth >80% of GPU mem for >2m
- follow up with CS about long-term product guidance (toolcall chunking + retry jitter)

jordan (cs): sending update to customers now. will collect requested logs. thanks team. :pray:

amelia (support): thanks — marking this Triage->Mitigated (canary stable). will reopen if we see further crashes.

inference-bot: [RESOLVE] upstream-runner crashloop on hosted-gpu-pool-07: mitigated by kv evict cap + reduced concurrency. Monitor window: 30m

sophia (sre): filing initial incident doc and assigning postmortem owners. I'll add timeline and links to PR/metrics.

devon (infra): follow-up: open issue infra#1127 for permanent kv accounting and eviction policy improvements.

raj (oncall): closing handover — if anyone sees 503 spikes after promotion, ping me directly.

amelia (support): thanks everyone.
